findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass field default, which is evaluated exactly once when the module is imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is created. Every instance created in a worker/web process therefore carries the process start-up timestamp, so the field is useless for reasoning about when the assignment was queued (and will drift arbitrarily far from reality in long-lived processes). Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: AssignmentSource does not round-trip through task kwargs (datetime `queued`)
findings.body: `to_dict()` uses `dataclasses.asdict`, which leaves `queued` as a raw `datetime`. This dict is passed as a Celery kwarg in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` (`assignment_source_dict=assignment_source.to_dict()`). With a JSON task serializer this either fails to serialize or is serialized as an ISO string; `from_dict` then does `cls(**input_dict)` with no coercion, producing an `AssignmentSource` whose `queued` is a `str` despite the declared `datetime` type. Either serialize/deserialize `queued` explicitly (e.g. `isoformat()` / `fromisoformat`) or drop the field from the wire format.

findings.title: from_dict silently returns None on malformed payload, disabling loop protection
findings.body: `from_dict` swallows `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None`. In `sync_assignee_outbound` a `None` source means `should_sync("outbound_assignee", None)` passes, so a malformed/renamed payload silently re-enables the sync cycle this PR is meant to break, with no log or metric to detect it. Log a warning (or raise) when a non-empty `assignment_source_dict` fails to parse.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to abstract `sync_status_outbound` but never used
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature now declares `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None`, but no caller in this PR passes it and the concrete provider implementations (Jira/VSTS/etc.) were not updated to accept or honor it. The parameter is dead and only reaches implementations through `**kwargs`, so the signature change implies status-sync loop protection that does not actually exist. Either wire it through (status inbound -> outbound) or drop it from the abstract signature.

findings.title: No test for the actual to_dict -> task kwargs -> from_dict round trip
findings.body: The tests only call `from_dict` with hand-written dicts that omit `queued`, and `to_dict` is asserted only to contain a non-None `queued`. The real production path is `to_dict()` -> Celery kwargs -> `from_dict()`, which is exactly where the `datetime`/string mismatch (and possible serializer failure) occurs. Add a test asserting `AssignmentSource.from_dict(source.to_dict()) == source`, including after JSON round-tripping, so the serialization contract used by `sync_assignee_outbound` is covered.
